solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A cub's a strange means of multiplying

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the preceding words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A young scout's odd way of doing his times tables.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame for counting is a traditional calculating device, used for multiplication as well as addition.

clue.text: Barracks heard binge

indicators.note: heard signals a word that sounds like the jeering word

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer, so barracks means boos

explanation.surface: Drinking noise overheard from soldiers' quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barracks' looks like army quarters but is a verb: jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy drinking session is a binge; the word also names alcohol and a drinking bout.

clue.text: Associate is devious to Le Carré

indicators.note: devious means the letters of the phrase take a winding, rearranged route

explanation.surface: A spy novelist's associate is shifty, as befits his fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: John le Carré is a writer of spy novels; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To link two things in the mind is to connect them, which is what associate means as a verb.

clue.text: Six in light bender raised whimper

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
in puts the Roman numeral inside the optical device

parts.note: a lens bends light
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sixth bender of light lifted makes a whimper.
explanation.walkthrough: VI in LENS gives LEVINS, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry feebly and complainingly is to whine, a synonym of whimper.

clue.text: Baggage handler's employment in seasonal work?

indicators.note: in places the word for employment inside the seasonal piece

parts.note: a carol is a Christmas song, a seasonal composition
employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: Suggests a porter's job is only seasonal work, like Christmas temping.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: At airports, luggage reaches passengers on a rotating conveyor belt, which handles the bags.

clue.text: Perhaps 1 evaluates retaliations?

parts.note: the answer to 1 across, a bead frame for reckoning, is one example of a counting device
measures means gauges or evaluates

explanation.surface: A device that sizes up revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' shows the 1-across answer is one example of the needed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Actions taken in response to a threat or attack are reprisals, or retaliations.

clue.text: Ukraine's capital subsequently piercing sky over mountainous region

indicators.note: piercing places the letters inside the turned-round sky
over in a down clue signals the word for sky turned upside down

parts.note: the air is the sky

indicators.note: capital picks the first letter of Ukraine

parts.note: then means subsequently, afterwards

explanation.surface: Ukraine's capital later piercing the sky above a mountainous area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Kyiv but means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This historical region of the Carpathians, now western Ukraine, is a mountainous area.

clue.text: For Florence, a room free of destructive devices

parts.note: una is Italian for a, so it is what a Florentine would say

explanation.surface: A Florentine room cleared of bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm means to free of weapons; destructive devices here means arms.

clue.text: Remedy caught for south in water off N Taiwan

indicators.note: for signals that one letter replaces another

parts.note: the East China Sea, written E China Sea, lies north of Taiwan
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cure caught in the sea off Taiwan.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coneflower used as a herbal medicine, especially against colds.

clue.text: Become quite agitated when grasping middle of boa constrictor

indicators.note: grasping means holding the boa's centre letter inside the word for become

parts.note: to turn can mean to become, as milk turns sour

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of boa
agitated means the letters of quite are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone panics as a boa constrictor tightens its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constrictor' looks like part of the snake, but it is the definition; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourniquet is a band tightened round a limb to stop bleeding, literally a device that squeezes.

clue.text: Hospital needed in great pain

indicators.note: needed in places the hospital abbreviation within the word for great

parts.note: ace means excellent, great
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient in agony urgently needs hospital treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous hurt is a pain, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Legendary rider not outwardly showing respect

parts.note: Paul Revere made the legendary midnight ride of 1775 warning of British troops

indicators.note: outwardly keeps only the outside letters of not

explanation.surface: A famous horseman shows no outward respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not outwardly' looks like a negation of the definition, but it supplies the end letters of 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deferential and full of awe is to be respectful, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Unusual name? No

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of name and no appear in an uncommon arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a name is not really unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the Irish forename, with its double N, is an unusual-looking name built from 'name no'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Irish male forename, the Gaelic form of Edmund, unfamiliar in spelling to many.

clue.text: Reduced a concrete sphere

indicators.note: reduced means the word for concrete is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: concrete means real, tangible

explanation.surface: A sphere made smaller and cast in concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: A field or domain of activity is a sphere, as in an area of expertise.

clue.text: Liberal in party man trashed without restraint

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the jumbled words
trashed means the letters of party man are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal at a party trashes the place wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting unchecked and wildly is doing things unrestrainedly, the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Frenetic manoeuvres give more complaints

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters of frenetic are moved about into new positions

explanation.surface: Frantic military exercises lead to more grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass illnesses on again is to infect once more; complaints here means ailments.

clue.text: Enthusiast traps popular banker

indicators.note: traps means the enthusiast word encloses the word for popular

parts.note: a fancier is an enthusiast, as in a pigeon fancier
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A fan catches a well-liked banker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who manages large sums of money or funds ventures is a banker in the broad sense.

clue.text: Czech beer (specifically and generally) hasn't succeeded for marauder

indicators.note: hasn't means the letter for succeeded is removed

parts.note: Pils is a Czech-style beer, specifically
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in genealogies
generally, a Czech beer is a lager

explanation.surface: A drinker's choice of beer causes a raider to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: '(specifically and generally)' says the beer is read twice: specifically PILS, generally LAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plunders and loots is a raider, a marauder.

clue.text: Stupid formality reversed in fleet with head dismissed

indicators.note: in places the turned-round formality inside the shortened word for fleet
with head dismissed removes the first letter of the word for fleet

parts.note: fleet means quick, nimble

indicators.note: reversed means the word for formality is read backwards

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, stiff formality

explanation.surface: A daft piece of etiquette is overturned in the navy when the admiral is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like a navy of ships but here is an adjective meaning swift; 'ice' as formality is a stiff, cold manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word means foolish or idiotic, a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Either way, use element in soda bread

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium, the element in soda

indicators.note: either way means the symbol is used forwards and then backwards

parts.note: the same sodium symbol, used a second time

explanation.surface: A baking instruction to use sodium in soda bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soda bread' looks like one phrase, but 'soda' belongs to the wordplay and 'bread' alone is the definition; 'use' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, a type of bread.

clue.text: Breathless, uplifting French from folios at university

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: de is French for from
ff is the abbreviation for folios
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Breathless after an uplifting session with French manuscripts at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of breath after exertion means panting, i.e. breathless.

clue.text: Launch periodical over spring

indicators.note: over signals that the combined words are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to launch or toss something high
mag is short for magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: Launching a magazine in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but it is a verb meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic about with leaps and skips is to jump or leap playfully.

clue.text: Coach welcomes representative birthday torment

indicators.note: welcomes means the coach takes in the representative

parts.note: a coach is a bus
MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A coach party greets an MP with a birthday ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British birthday tradition, friends lift the birthday person and thump them on the ground, once per year of age.
explanation.definitionFit: This playground birthday ritual of repeated thumps is a good-natured torment.

clue.text: Initially stall for time when British weaponry is returned, being well-protected

indicators.note: for signals that one letter takes the place of another
is returned means the weapons are read backwards

parts.note: Sten guns were British submachine guns of the Second World War

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of stall

explanation.surface: Someone stalls for time once British arms are handed back, keeping themselves safe.
explanation.walkthrough: STENGUNS read backwards gives SNUGNETS; its T for time becomes S, the first letter of 'stall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being snug means being cosily sheltered, so the noun names the state of being well protected.

clue.text: Fault American hollowness

parts.note: a sin is a fault or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Blaming American emptiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically this is a cavity in bone, a hollow space; the clue uses hollowness for hollow.

clue.text: Bit of excitement for pair possibly including …

indicators.note: bit of means a run of letters taken from within the word excitement

explanation.surface: A little thrill for a couple who might include the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to the next clue: the couple may include one partner's steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple in a romantic relationship is called this word informally, so it is a pair.

clue.text: … steady backing equipment to supply around weekday

indicators.note: backing means the word for equipment is written backwards

parts.note: rig is a set of equipment, such as a drilling rig

indicators.note: around has the word for supply going round the day

parts.note: to lend is to supply, furnish
Fri is the short form of Friday

explanation.surface: Someone steadily backs up equipment provision around a working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steady' here is a noun, the regular partner, completing the thought begun in the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular romantic partner; a female partner fits that sense.

clue.text: Mine finally agreed its outputs produce carbuncles

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of mine

parts.note: yes is the word of agreement
a mine's outputs are its ores, the minerals extracted

explanation.surface: A mine's agreed production results in boils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbuncles' suggests boils, but means ugly buildings, as in Prince Charles's 'monstrous carbuncle' remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly buildings that spoil a view are called carbuncles, so both mean unsightly blots.

clue.text: Force club subscription with society overcoming resistance

indicators.note: overcoming has the subscription word surrounding the resistance symbol

parts.note: dues are a member's subscription fees
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A club forces up its fees after members resist.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion by threats is compulsion, which is force applied to make someone act.
